record.one_liner: Lark is ByteDance's international workplace suite combining chat, calendar, docs, email, video meetings, approvals and a developer platform.
record.auth_notes: Custom apps POST app_id and app_secret to /open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal and get a tenant_access_token (valid up to 2 hours). Calls send it as "Authorization: Bearer <token>". user_access_token is obtained through an OAuth authorization-code flow, which the MCP README describes with a redirect URL and offline_access scope. I could not fetch the OAuth doc pages, so the user-token flow details are not verified from Lark docs. Marketplace apps use app_access_token, which I did not verify.
record.access_notes: Creating a custom app in the developer console is self-serve and free, but I did not fetch a page that states the cost. Scopes can be tested without review in a test enterprise, or without review for scopes that support user_access_token. For production, the app version must be submitted and approved by an admin, and per the scopes doc, API permissions take effect only after approval. Some scopes are no-review. Marketplace (store) apps additionally go through Lark review. The doc is inconsistent about whether the app admin or the tenant admin approves.
record.blocker: Production use needs tenant admin approval of the app version and its scopes. Message sending is rate limited (1,000/min and 50/sec per API, 5 QPS per user or group). Feishu (China) and Lark (international) are separate tenants and apps are not interchangeable. The official MCP is in Beta and does not support file upload/download or direct document editing.
